brief: JPM's morning briefing frames the session as geopolitics-led: oil, global yields and volatility extended higher, with Brent testing $110 overnight on Iran resuming ballistic missile production and Houthis nearing Bab al-Mandeb, then paring as Iran and Gulf states were reported to meet Monday on a Hormuz deal. The ECB's hike, which JPM and the market read as surprisingly hawkish, added to the rates selloff, leaving a near-full October hike and roughly 90bp of tightening priced over the next year, while JPM Econ keeps a December hike call. US CPI is today's focus after headline PPI rose 0.4%m/m and JPM's early core PCE estimate is 0.20%m/m. Tech is a macro input: Research attributes 0.2%pt of global core CPI to it, and behind-the-meter datacenter power is a rising theme with 75GW of orders tracked. Equity monetization stays tactically cautious and neutral globally, long US and Asia versus Europe, hedged on momentum, high conviction short EU Chemicals and Asia Consumer Electronics, bullish EM with country-relative trades. Positioning shows hedge funds re-grossing while sentiment turns less constructive.
